about: Edition 10 (after the storm) of storm-charles.promptugal.news's decision brief on Storm Charles: the words and judgements of this edition (the lead, what to watch, the authorities' decisions, sources compared). The figures (warnings, observations, flights, notices) are drawn by tools/brief-make.mjs from the incident's data files as they stood at the as-of time. Every item is labelled fact, evidence or hypothesis and carries its source and the time read. Not a warning service: IPMA issues the warnings and ANEPC the instructions.
next: This is the after-the-storm edition. A further edition only if IPMA issues a new warning for Lisbon or the authorities publish their own final figures.

lead.label: fact
lead.text: Storm Charles has passed Lisbon. Its last warning above yellow, the orange sea, ended at 21:00; yellow sea runs to 03:00 Thursday. Lisbon had red rain from 09:00 to 15:00, ended early (it ran to 18:00), and an orange wind ended early at 15:56; the red wind first issued for Wednesday was lowered at 07:16. At 20:00 the airport observed west 17 km/h and 996 hPa, rising.

src.name: IPMA's CAP messages via MeteoAlarm (read 21:00, timeline s-1111T2100)

lead.label: fact
lead.text: What Lisbon got: about 110 mm of rain on Wednesday at Relógio (in the hours we hold), 74 mm of it in six hours to the hour labelled 14:00; the heaviest single hour 26.2 mm at Oeiras (13:00). The strongest gust at the airport was 74 km/h, at 14:00, below the 120 km/h of the orange warning and the 140 km/h of the red first issued.

lead.label: evidence
lead.text: Civil protection's 19:00 briefing, as the press relays it: 1,630 occurrences on the mainland since midnight, 781 of them floods, most in Greater Lisbon, the Setúbal Peninsula and the Algarve; one person assisted and four removed from their homes; "much less serious than forecast". About 400 flights were cancelled at Lisbon, Porto, Faro and Madeira (Lusa).

src.name: CNN Portugal relaying ANEPC; Lusa (timeline s-1111T2003, s-1111T1946)

watch.label: fact
watch.text: Lisbon: yellow sea (waves 4 to 5 m) to 03:00 Thursday; nothing above yellow.

watch.label: fact
watch.text: No IPMA warning for Lisbon above yellow. The airport forecast (17:00): showers at times, south-west gusts of about 50 km/h from 10:00 to 18:00.

watch.label: evidence
watch.text: Web Summit reported reopening for its last day, with many of Wednesday's sessions rescheduled and a press conference at 11:00 (the press, with Lusa); the organisers' own accounts have posted nothing since 10 November 17:36.

watch.label: evidence
watch.text: The Interior Ministry expects normality to resume; the alert situation ends at 23:59 tonight.

watch.label: fact
watch.text: Still interrupted when last read: CP's Lisbon trains between Campolide and Alcântara Terra (Carris routes 713 and 751 as CP's alternative), and the Beira Baixa line between Entroncamento and Abrantes after a landslip.

signs.label: hypothesis
signs.text: Nothing in the data points to a second peak for Lisbon tonight (our meteorologist, high confidence); Thursday looks like showers and a south-west wind.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Lisbon's orange sea warning ended at 21:00 as set; yellow sea to 03:00. Its last message, at 19:17:31, ended yellow rain early in Guarda, Bragança and Vila Real.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Lisbon's yellow rain ended at 18:00; the orange wind had ended early at 15:56; no red on the mainland since 15:56.

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: The Prime Minister: the moments of greatest difficulty are "practically overcome"; the alert situation ends at 23:59; normality expected Thursday.

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: 1,630 occurrences on the mainland since midnight, 781 floods; one person assisted, four removed from their homes; "much less serious than forecast".

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Both Lisbon bridges back to normal: usual limits restored; motorcycles and high-sided vehicles may cross.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Trafaria – Porto Brandão – Belém back to normal, vehicles and passengers.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Douro line running again; Beira Baixa interrupted between Entroncamento and Abrantes; Lisbon's Campolide – Alcântara Terra trains still suppressed.

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: Day 3 reopens on Thursday 12 November, "the busiest Thursday ever"; some of Wednesday's sessions move to Thursday. Reported by 24 Notícias and Público from the organisers' message to participants; not read at the organisers' own page.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Alert situation for the whole mainland, Wednesday 00:00 to 23:59: schools and non-essential public services closed; outdoor events suspended.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Day 2 (Wednesday) will not take place, on the government's formal advice; Day 3 (Thursday) "aims to proceed as planned".

compare.official: IPMA (via Lusa, 19:34): the prevention measures matched the forecasts
compare.obs: Rain heavy as warned; wind well below the levels warned
compare.press: ANEPC: "much less serious than forecast"; the PM: "practically overcome"
compare.assessment: The rain was as warned and the wind much weaker; both the warnings and the stand-down followed the observations.

compare.official: Lowered to yellow and green on IPMA's warnings page (12:24); earlier red rain to 06:00, orange wind to 12:00
compare.obs: 249.5 mm in six hours at Areeiro (01:00–06:00); airport wind dropped from 89 km/h gusts at 07:00 to 13 km/h at 08:00
compare.press: Regional president: 479 mm somewhere on the island; 205 occurrences, none serious
compare.assessment: The worst has passed Madeira; the risk now is what the rain left (slopes, streams), which only the regional civil protection can state.

change: After the storm. Lisbon's last warning above yellow, the orange sea, ended at 21:00 as IPMA set it; only yellow sea remains, to 03:00 Thursday. No red warning on the mainland since 15:56; IPMA's last message, at 19:17, ended yellow rain early in Guarda, Bragança and Vila Real. This edition sets what was forecast and warned beside what was observed, and what was decided beside how it ended.
ana: About 400 flights cancelled at Lisbon, Porto, Faro and Madeira on Wednesday (Lusa, 19:30); at Lisbon, 288 had been cancelled in advance by 11:00 (the airports' operator's own figures).

after.forecast: Red, "strong and persistent", 09:00 to 18:00 (issued Tuesday, moved three hours earlier on Tuesday night); shortened at 12:33 to end at 15:00, then yellow to 18:00
after.observed: Heavy from about 07:00 to 14:00: 74 mm in six hours at Relógio, the heaviest hour 26.2 mm at Oeiras (13:00); in the hour labelled 15:00, 0 to 1.2 mm
after.verdict: The red warning sat on the heaviest rain of the storm; IPMA ended it as the rain eased.

after.forecast: Red for Wednesday 12:00 to 21:00, gusts to 140 km/h (Tuesday); lowered at 07:16 to orange 09:00 to 21:00, gusts to 120; shortened to 18:00 at 12:33; ended at 15:56
after.observed: Highest gust at the airport 74 km/h at 14:00, as the centre passed; 50 km/h at 18:00 in the turn to west-north-west
after.verdict: The wind came well below every level warned; IPMA lowered and then ended the warning as the observations came in.

after.forecast: Communiqué no. 2: most likely between Sines and Cabo Carvoeiro, high uncertainty; ECMWF ensemble (11:57): 49% of forecasts south of Lisbon, 41% near, 10% north; our meteorologist: just north (09:22), possibly south (11:28), over or just south (12:24), just north (14:25)
after.observed: The wind backed to east-north-east by noon, turned to south at 14:00 with a 2 °C rise, then to west by 16:30 with the pressure rising from 989 hPa
after.verdict: The centre passed close to Lisbon, most likely just to the north; "near" in the ensemble's terms. Two centres (communiqué no. 3) weakened it.

after.forecast: Worst window 12:00 to 18:00 (the warnings' overlap); the ensemble's median crossing about 15:00
after.observed: Rain heaviest 11:00 to 14:00; the strongest gust 14:00; the turn to west-north-west 16:30 to 17:00
after.verdict: Earlier than the warning windows by one to three hours; the end came early too.

after.forecast: Orange, waves 5 to 7 m, up to 13 m, 12:00 to 21:00; modelled high water about 15:10
after.observed: No buoy or tide gauge in our data; ferries and the Algés seafront were restricted, the Trafaria crossing stopped vehicles
after.verdict: We cannot set the sea against an observation of our own: a gap for the next storm.

after.forecast: Red rain overnight to 06:00, orange wind to 12:00 (130 km/h in the mountains)
after.observed: 249.5 mm in six hours at Areeiro (01:00 to 06:00); the regional civil protection counted 325 occurrences to 18:40 (press)
after.verdict: Madeira had the storm's heaviest rain, before the mainland; its warnings matched it.

after.forecast: 4.93 million residents under red at noon (eight districts)
after.observed: Lowered to four districts at 12:19, two at 15:00, one at 15:06, none at 15:56
after.verdict: The red came off district by district through the afternoon, as the storm weakened.

after_src: Warnings: IPMA's open data and CAP messages; observations: IPMA's stations and the airport's METAR; the ensemble: ECMWF via Open-Meteo (incident.datascience@); the track readings: incident.meteorology@'s analysis (sections 12 to 28). Editions 1 to 9 show each of them as they stood.
lessons: IPMA's CAP messages led its open data by up to about two hours on Wednesday (12:18, 12:33, 15:55): a brief drawn from the open data alone would have been late each time.
The press repeated superseded warnings more than once (eight districts in red, Faro still red at 16:40, a red wind withdrawn at 07:16): read the warning at its source before comparing.
We hold no sea or tide observation; the next storm needs a tide gauge or buoy reading at its own source.
